events.summary: Chest image: This chest X-ray of a 48-year-old woman may show an enlarged heart and signs of fluid in the lungs, which fits the reference labels of Cardiomegaly and Edema.

limitations: This is one front-view (AP) picture read by an AI model, not by a radiologist; a qualified radiologist must review any real clinical image.
No prior X-rays are available for comparison, so it is not possible to say whether findings are new or long-standing.
Clinical information such as symptoms, lab results, or history is not available here and would be needed for any real medical decision.
uncertainty: AP portable X-rays can make the heart look bigger than it really is because of the angle the picture is taken from, so the heart size finding may not be fully reliable.
The hazy areas in the lungs could have more than one cause; fluid (edema) is one possibility but not the only one.
The reference labels were made by automated text-mining of a report and are sometimes wrong.

findings.statement: The heart shadow looks wider than usual relative to the chest width, which could suggest the heart is enlarged.
findings.evidence: The cardiac silhouette appears to occupy more than half the width of the chest on this AP portable view, consistent with the dataset label 'Cardiomegaly'.

findings.statement: There are hazy, cloudy areas in both lungs, especially toward the lower and middle zones, which may point to fluid building up in the lung tissue.
findings.evidence: Increased whitish haziness and indistinct lung markings visible bilaterally, consistent with the dataset label 'Edema'.

findings.statement: Several monitoring wires and what appears to be a pacemaker or implanted device are visible, suggesting the patient is being closely watched in a medical setting.
findings.evidence: Visible ECG leads, a device with leads in the right chest area, and 'PORTABLE' marker on the image.

red_flags.description: The chest X-ray label shows fluid in the lungs (pulmonary edema)

events.summary: A critical finding needs review by a healthcare professional before any guidance is given
Heart rhythm: The heart tracing shows a heart rate in the normal range, but the machine flagged several things that a doctor should look at.

limitations: The machine-generated report was NOT confirmed by a cardiologist; ECG machine reports are known to be over-cautious and can flag things that turn out to be normal.
Automatic beat counting on this trace was not reliable; the heart rate comes from the dataset value only.
Only 4 of the 12 ECG leads are shown in the picture, so a full assessment of the tracing is not possible here.
No clinical information about the person (age, symptoms, medical history) was provided, which is needed to put these findings in context.
uncertainty: It is uncertain whether the rhythm changes (called 'sinus arrhythmia') are harmless normal variation or something more significant without a doctor reviewing the full tracing.
The QRS axis of 124 degrees points to 'right axis deviation', but what this means for this person's health is uncertain without clinical context.
The machine report mentions a possible old heart attack ('inferior infarct - age undetermined'), but it is not known if this is real or a false alarm — only a cardiologist can say.

findings.statement: The heart rate is 85 beats per minute, which is within the normal resting range of about 60–100 beats per minute.

The electrical signal that spreads through the lower chambers of the heart takes longer than usual to travel — this is called a 'right bundle branch block', meaning one of the heart's electrical pathways may be delayed.
findings.evidence: qrs_ms: 140 (normal is under about 120 ms); machine report: 'Right bundle branch block'

findings.statement: The machine also flagged possible signs of reduced blood flow or injury in parts of the heart muscle, which could be important and needs a doctor to check.
findings.evidence: machine report: 'Inferior infarct - age undetermined | Lateral ST-T changes suggest myocardial injury/ischemia | Abnormal ECG'

red_flags.description: The ECG report mentions possible acute heart muscle injury
